# KafkaJMXScrapeSlow

<!-- GENERATED by monitoring/dashgen from internal/rules (make alerts). Do not edit. -->

| Severity | Component | Dashboard | for (production / demo) |
|---|---|---|---|
| warning | platform | [lab-monitoring](http://grafana.localhost:8080/d/lab-monitoring/) | 15m / 2m |

**Summary:** JMX scrape of broker <kafka_broker> takes more than 25 % of the 15 s scrape interval

The JMX exporter runs inside the broker JVM; slow scrapes cost broker CPU and hold MBean server locks. Check the allowlist (docs/metrics-performance-impact.md): new per-topic or per-client beans, or an overloaded broker.

## Impact

The JMX exporter consumes broker CPU and holds MBean locks for a large share of every scrape interval; scrapes may time out and dashboards show gaps.

## Diagnosis

1. Kafka Lab · Monitoring Overhead: did samples per scrape grow (new topics → per-topic beans)?
2. Is the broker itself overloaded (CPU throttling, GC)? A slow scrape is then a symptom.
3. See docs/metrics-performance-impact.md for the cost of each MBean group.

## Mitigation

- Narrow includeObjectNames in monitoring/bundle/jmx/kafka-jmx-exporter.yaml (e.g. drop per-topic BrokerTopicMetrics, fewer RequestMetrics request types).
- Raise the scrape interval for brokers (30 s) if you cannot reduce beans.

## Expression

```promql
max by (kafka_cluster, kafka_broker) (avg_over_time(jmx_scrape_duration_seconds[5m])) > 3.75
```
